complexity_scope.guarantee: Uniform per-instance success at least 1/2 is required; a fixed valid instance defeats each insufficient-budget algorithm with success below 1/2.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: Positive absolute numerical constants independent of all displayed parameters; constants may change under the smooth-to-Goldstein specialization.
complexity_scope.oracle: Exact scalar values of a fixed sampled function per handle; independent fresh handles, arbitrary same-handle reuse, all query points in known X.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: xout in X; ambient Goldstein residual G_delta(f,xout)<=epsilon.
complexity_scope.regime: epsilon<=cL0; Delta>=C delta epsilon; d>=C[1+log(2+Delta L0²/(delta epsilon³))]; constructed R=Theta(Delta/epsilon).
complexity_scope.resource: Scalar evaluations, with an all-transcript deterministic cap N; independent sample count is not the resource.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Every measurable randomized adaptive reusable-handle algorithm, including arbitrary unqueried outputs in X.

map: Import Theorem 4.1: under eta<=c0L0, HDelta>=C0 eta² and d>=C0[1+log(2+HDelta L0²/eta⁴)], a deterministic R=Theta(Delta/eta) supports globally H-smooth means, local gap Delta and sample Lipschitz second moment L0², each with an exact stationary point; every randomized reusable-handle algorithm with all-path cap N<=cN dL0²HDelta/eta⁴ fails on some fixed member with probability greater than 1/2.

Section 5 constructs disjoint Gaussian hidden rooms plus a linear carrier and terminal cancellation bump. On G={max_j||U_j||<=2}, Lemma 5.1 and Appendix B establish model membership and ||grad f||>eta outside the terminal room, while grad f at its center is zero.

Lemma 6.1 retains one fixed Gaussian noise vector for each handle/room. After Gram–Schmidt, posterior covariance is n^(-1)(I+sigma^(-2)sum_h P_h)^(-1), with q=sum_h rank(P_h) increasing by at most one per scalar observation.
Lemma 6.2: q<q0=floor(n sigma²/16) leaves at least 3n/4 covariance eigenvalues >=4/(5n), so every transcript-measurable estimator misses radius 1/16 except with probability exp(-cn).

Section 6.2 uses a shadow transcript suppressing unresolved future bumps, never conditioning on previous misses. Clock separation selects at most one future room per proposal. A hit estimates the current hidden direction within 1/16. Lemma 6.3 and a union bound cover N queries and the final output with probability <=(N+1)exp(-cn).

True and shadow experiments share pre-sampled directions, handle noises and seed and agree until a future hit. N<Mq0 cannot unlock M directions. The source proves P(success intersect G)<=(N+1)exp(-cn), not an unconditional terminal-room implication for invalid Gaussian realizations. P(G)>=7/8 and the dimension condition give E[p_A(U)|G]<=2/7<1/2, hence a fixed valid bad instance.
M=Theta(HDelta/eta²), q0=Theta(dL0²/eta²); their product yields the imported smooth lower bound.

proofs.full_local_argument: For globally H-Lipschitz grad f and any finite convex combination g=sum_i lambda_i grad f(y_i), with ||y_i-x||<=delta, lambda_i>=0 and sum_i lambda_i=1, triangle inequality gives ||grad f(x)||<=||g||+sum_i lambda_i||grad f(x)-grad f(y_i)||<=||g||+Hdelta. Continuity of norm extends this to the closed convex hull defining partial_delta f(x); taking the infimum gives ||grad f(x)||<=G_delta(f,x)+Hdelta. Thus G_delta<=epsilon implies ||grad f||<=2epsilon when H=epsilon/delta. Apply the imported smooth interface with eta=2epsilon: eta<=c0L0 becomes epsilon<=cL0; HDelta>=C0eta² becomes Delta>=C delta epsilon; HDelta L0²/eta⁴=Delta L0²/(16 delta epsilon³), absorbed into absolute constants in the logarithmic dimension threshold. Its scalar budget is cN dL0²(epsilon/delta)Delta/(2epsilon)^4=(cN/16)dL0²Delta/(delta epsilon³). Every Goldstein-success output is therefore a smooth-success output on that hard family, so the same fixed bad instance defeats it. R=Theta(Delta/eta)=Theta(Delta/epsilon). The terminal center has zero gradient and hence is Clarke stationary, preserving the existence promise. All queries, handle reuse and output permissions are unchanged.

assumptions: d is an integer at least 2; L0,Delta,delta,epsilon>0.
There are absolute c,C>0 such that epsilon<=c L0, Delta>=C delta epsilon, and d>=C[1+log(2+Delta L0²/(delta epsilon³))].

A new opaque handle receives an independent draw xi_h from the same fixed law. At each evaluation both retained handle h and point x in X may be chosen adaptively from the complete transcript. Feedback is exactly F(x;xi_h). Handles may be retained and reused arbitrarily; each scalar evaluation costs one. Creating an unevaluated handle is free and uninformative.

Output lies in X and may be a point never queried. The budget is at most N evaluations on every transcript, not merely an expected budget. The algorithm knows the stationary-point existence promise but not its location.
statement.conclusion: For the constructed R, N_G^stat(d,R,L0,Delta,delta,epsilon)>=c d L0² Delta/(delta epsilon³). The lower bound survives arbitrary repeated evaluations of retained sample handles.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Let X=B_2^d(0,R) be a known closed ball. A jointly measurable F:R^d x Xi -> R has E|F(0;xi)|<infinity. On one common full-measure event, |F(x;xi)-F(y;xi)|<=L(xi)||x-y|| for all ambient x,y, with E L(xi)^2<=L0². Set f=E F and require f(0)-min_X f<=Delta. Define partial_delta f(x)=cl conv union_{||y-x||<=delta} partial^C f(y) and G_delta(f,x)=dist_2(0,partial_delta f(x)). The union is ambient, not truncated to X. N_G^stat is the least integer all-transcript scalar budget for one randomized algorithm to produce xout in X with P(G_delta(f,xout)<=epsilon)>=1/2 uniformly over this class restricted to instances having some xstar in X with 0 in partial^C f(xstar).
statement.parameter_domains: The regime above with absolute constants; R is constructed, not an arbitrary independently prescribed radius. The hard means are globally smooth C-infinity functions, specialized with H=epsilon/delta and eta=2epsilon.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every admissible parameter tuple there exists a deterministic radius R=Theta(Delta/epsilon) and a valid smooth instance family, every member having a stationary point in X. For every adaptive randomized reusable-handle algorithm with sufficiently small budget N<=c' d L0² Delta/(delta epsilon³), there is a fixed member of this family on which its success probability is below 1/2. Probability includes independent handle draws and internal algorithm randomness; the fixed instance does not depend on the realized seed or transcript.
